payload.writeUp: Claude Code research, 23 Oct 2026: UK equity crowdfunding campaigns (Crowdcube, Republic Europe). The platforms block automated reading, so no round here is confirmed open: claims come from the companies' own sites, Companies House and TechRound's weekly crowdfunding round-ups (31 Aug–5 Oct 2026), with the platform page kept as the investment link. SEIS/EIS is as reported by TechRound, not from an advance-assurance letter. A member should open the platform page to confirm the round is live.

candidate.name: SEPANTA
candidate.subSector: AI operating system and governed agents
candidate.teaser: London AI company (formerly Goodfolio) selling governed AI systems to enterprises; crowdfunding on Crowdcube with EIS.
candidate.description: SEPANTA sells an 'AI operating system for growth' plus ready-made applications (Finspector, NuStream, GoodMora, GoodProcess) and custom governed agents, according to its website. IT Brief UK (5 Oct 2026) reports the company signed seven enterprise contracts in a month including one six-figure deal, says it has generated more than £1m revenue to date, and grew without institutional VC using customer revenue, angel investment and crowdfunding. TechRound listed it as raising on Crowdcube with EIS in the week of 5 October 2026, and its own homepage embeds a Crowdcube campaign banner. Round size and valuation were not visible to us. Risks: crowded enterprise-AI market, services-heavy delivery, and repeated crowdfunding rounds may mean dilution.
candidate.discoverySignal: TechRound crowdfunding roundup w/c 5 Oct 2026 lists SEPANTA on Crowdcube (EIS); company homepage carries a live Crowdcube banner.
candidate.researchRuleMatched: Live EIS equity crowdfunding round with a platform route for individuals

founders.name: Omid Pakseresht
founders.bio: Chief Executive Officer of SEPANTA, quoted by IT Brief UK on the company's enterprise contract wins.

access.notes: Crowdcube campaign (pitch link taken from the Crowdcube banner embedded on sepanta.io). Crowdcube blocked automated reading, so status and terms were not verified.

eis.note: TechRound roundup lists 'SEIS/EIS? Yes, EIS'. Advance assurance not seen directly.

facts.label: Recent contracts
facts.value: Seven new enterprise contracts in the past month, one six-figure

signals.headline: Seven enterprise deals in a month
signals.summary: IT Brief UK reports SEPANTA signed seven enterprise contracts in the past month including one six-figure deal.

openQuestions: What is the round target, pre-money valuation and amount committed?
How much revenue is recurring software vs consulting/services?
Why 'three crowdfunding rounds' rather than institutional funding, and what is the cap table?

assessment.summary: Revenue-generating enterprise-AI firm with a live Crowdcube EIS round, but valuation and terms unseen and the market is crowded.
whyInterested: Reported £1m+ revenue to date without institutional VC
risks: Multiple prior crowdfunding rounds may mean a fragmented cap table
assessment.bullCase: Governed-agent platform becomes sticky across enterprise clients and converts services work into recurring software revenue.
assessment.bearCase: Remains a consultancy-style AI integrator competing with large SIs and platforms, with limited multiple expansion.
assessment.whyNow: Campaign listed as live on Crowdcube in October 2026.
diligenceChecklist: Read the live campaign page and offer documents in full
Confirm HMRC advance assurance letter (SEIS/EIS) with the company
Check latest Companies House accounts and confirmation statement
Confirm share class, rights and any nominee structure on the platform
assessment.nextAction: Open the Crowdcube pitch and note valuation, target, revenue split and days left.

candidate.name: Stablepharma
candidate.teaser: Developing fridge-free vaccines via its StablevaX platform; crowdfunding on Crowdcube with EIS.
candidate.description: Stablepharma's StablevaX platform reformulates vaccines and pharmaceuticals into thermostable forms it says remain safe and effective at 40°C and above; its lead programme is a tetanus-diphtheria vaccine (SPVX02). The website states it was awarded a €2.5m EIC Accelerator grant and displays 'We're crowdfunding!' with a link to a Crowdcube pitch. TechRound listed it raising on Crowdcube with EIS in the week of 7 September 2026. Companies House shows the company incorporated in 2012 (registered office Exeter). Risks: long, expensive clinical and regulatory path; later-stage than the family's ideal; round size and valuation not seen.
candidate.discoverySignal: Company homepage says 'We're crowdfunding!' linking to a Crowdcube pitch; TechRound roundup w/c 7 Sep 2026 lists it with EIS.
candidate.researchRuleMatched: Live EIS crowdfunding round (later-stage exception: deep-tech biotech)

founders.name: Özgür Tuncer
founders.bio: Two decades in the biopharmaceutical industry including Pfizer, IQVIA and Pharmacia, per the company team page.

founders.name: Nick Child
founders.bio: Described on the team page as an experienced company leader and business developer in UK and international markets.

access.notes: Pitch link is on the company homepage. Crowdcube blocked automated reading, so live status and terms were not verified.

eis.note: TechRound roundup lists 'Yes, EIS'. Advance assurance not seen directly.

openQuestions: What valuation is this round at, and how does it compare with earlier rounds?
What is the timeline and funding need to complete SPVX02 clinical development?
Who are the institutional investors in the round, if any?

assessment.summary: Credible deep-tech biotech with grant validation and an experienced pharma team, but later-stage than ideal and valuation unseen.
risks: Capital intensive; heavy future dilution likely
assessment.bullCase: Thermostable platform licensed to major vaccine makers, with SPVX02 approval validating it.
assessment.bearCase: Clinical delays and funding gaps dilute crowd investors before any licensing event.
assessment.whyNow: Company is actively crowdfunding on Crowdcube.
diligenceChecklist: Read the live campaign page and offer documents in full
Confirm HMRC advance assurance letter (SEIS/EIS) with the company
Check latest Companies House accounts and confirmation statement
Confirm share class, rights and any nominee structure on the platform
assessment.nextAction: Open the Crowdcube pitch to check valuation, use of funds and clinical milestones.

candidate.name: 0rCA (formerly Fishy Filaments)
candidate.teaser: Cornish company turning end-of-life fishing nets into PA6 nylon with a containerised recycling plant; small EIS Crowdcube raise.
candidate.description: 0rCA (formerly Fishy Filaments) recycles end-of-life fishing nets into PA6 nylon, and is building '0rCA in a Container', a containerised recycling system designed to sit near where nets are discarded. Its website cites 6,102 kg of nets recovered and 14 fishing boats serviced, and says a GB patent was granted in 2025 on the process and hardware. TechRound listed a Crowdcube raise of £52,668 with EIS in the week of 28 September 2026. Companies House shows Fishy Filaments Limited incorporated in 2017 in Penryn, Cornwall. Risks: small scale so far, hardware roll-out economics unproven, valuation not verified.
candidate.discoverySignal: TechRound roundup w/c 28 Sep 2026 lists a £52,668 Crowdcube raise with EIS.
candidate.researchRuleMatched: Live EIS crowdfunding round, small raise, climate hardware

access.notes: Crowdcube campaign reported by TechRound; Crowdcube blocked automated reading so status not verified.

facts.label: Patent
facts.value: GB patent granted 2025 on process and hardware (company timeline)

openQuestions: What pre-money valuation is the Crowdcube round at? (a search snippet suggested about £7.5m; unverified)
Unit economics of one containerised plant
Revenue to date and customer pipeline for recycled PA6

assessment.summary: Genuine circular-economy story with a patent and small EIS raise, but early commercial traction is thin and valuation unverified.
whyInterested: Small raise where a family cheque would be material
risks: Valuation may be high relative to traction
assessment.bullCase: Containerised plants licensed or sold to ports globally create a scalable network.
assessment.bearCase: Remains a niche materials supplier with limited volumes.
assessment.whyNow: Small Crowdcube round reported live in late September 2026.
diligenceChecklist: Read the live campaign page and offer documents in full
Confirm HMRC advance assurance letter (SEIS/EIS) with the company
Check latest Companies House accounts and confirmation statement
Confirm share class, rights and any nominee structure on the platform
assessment.nextAction: Check the Crowdcube page for valuation and whether the round is still open; ask about container unit economics.

candidate.name: Foundermatcha
candidate.teaser: App that matches founders with tech co-founders, engineers and advisors using personality and working-style data; SEIS raise on Republic.
candidate.description: Foundermatcha is a matchmaking platform and app that pairs founders with engineers, technical co-founders and advisors, matching on personality, working style and equity-versus-cash expectations, per its website. TechRound listed a £200,027 Republic Europe raise with SEIS in the week of 21 September 2026, and the company website still shows an 'Invest In Foundermatcha' link to its Republic page. Companies House shows Foundermatcha Ltd incorporated November 2022 (London). Risks: consumer-style marketplace with unclear monetisation, campaign may already have closed.
candidate.discoverySignal: TechRound roundup w/c 21 Sep 2026 lists a £200,027 SEIS raise on Republic Europe; website links to the Republic campaign.
candidate.researchRuleMatched: SEIS pre-seed crowdfunding round with a platform route

access.notes: Republic Europe campaign linked from the company site. Republic blocked automated reading; the campaign may have closed (approved late August 2026).

openQuestions: Is the Republic round still open, and at what pre-money valuation?
How does Foundermatcha make money (subscriptions, fees)?
How many active users and matches are there? (the site counters did not render for us)

assessment.summary: Small SEIS raise for a founder-matching app; interesting niche but monetisation and traction unclear and the round may have closed.
whyInterested: Small round where cheques are meaningful
assessment.bullCase: Becomes the default UK route to assemble founding teams, monetised via subscriptions and accelerator partnerships.
assessment.bearCase: Low willingness to pay and competition from free tools cap growth.
diligenceChecklist: Read the live campaign page and offer documents in full
Confirm HMRC advance assurance letter (SEIS/EIS) with the company
Check latest Companies House accounts and confirmation statement
Confirm share class, rights and any nominee structure on the platform
assessment.nextAction: Check whether the Republic campaign is still open; if so, request traction and revenue metrics.

candidate.name: The Football Factory (TFF)
candidate.teaser: Plans to combine football clubs, real estate and AI into investable 'football citadels'; SEIS campaign in pre-registration on Republic.
candidate.description: TFF describes itself as an investment and operating ecosystem combining football, real estate and AI, aiming to build 'Europe's first Football Citadel' and replicate it across three more clubs in three countries. Its investors page says the crowdfunding campaign has launched in pre-registration mode on Republic; TechRound listed a £100,000 SEIS raise in the week of 31 August 2026. Companies House shows THEFOOTBALLFACTORY LTD (no. 17166985) with founder and CEO Edoardo Giacone appointed director in April 2026, resident in Italy. Risks: very early, capital-intensive real-estate thesis, UK company with mainly European operations, speculative.
candidate.discoverySignal: Company investors page says the Republic campaign is in pre-registration; TechRound w/c 31 Aug 2026 lists a £100,000 SEIS raise.

founders.name: Edoardo Giacone
founders.bio: Founder and CEO per the company website; describes years closing deals across European football. Director of THEFOOTBALLFACTORY LTD since April 2026.

access.notes: Company says the Republic campaign is in pre-registration ('coming soon'). Register interest on Republic.

openQuestions: Where will the first 'Football Citadel' be, and what assets does the UK company own?
How can a £100k SEIS raise fund a real-estate-heavy plan?
Which clubs, if any, have signed agreements?

assessment.summary: Ambitious, highly speculative football-plus-real-estate concept at pre-registration; tiny SEIS round versus a capital-heavy plan.
risks: Capital-intensive thesis far beyond the round size
Newly incorporated UK entity with overseas operations
assessment.bullCase: Signs a first club partnership and attracts institutional real-estate capital, lifting early equity value.
assessment.bearCase: Concept never secures assets and the SEIS equity is heavily diluted or lost.
diligenceChecklist: Read the live campaign page and offer documents in full
Confirm HMRC advance assurance letter (SEIS/EIS) with the company
Check latest Companies House accounts and confirmation statement
Confirm share class, rights and any nominee structure on the platform
assessment.nextAction: Only register interest if the family wants a speculative sports bet; ask for signed club agreements first.

candidate.description: Evogro supplies internet-connected hydroponic growing cabinets, support services and consumables so restaurants, hotels and bars can grow salad leaves, microgreens and herbs on site, according to its website. candidate.name: VEYR
candidate.teaser: AI fitness app that builds workouts around a user's time, kit and energy; £1m round at £4.5m pre-money incl. £400k via Crowdcube.
candidate.description: VEYR is an AI fitness app whose 'Fitness Intelligence Engine' generates and adapts workouts to a user's goals, equipment, time and energy. A company press release (27 July 2026) announced a £1m round at a £4.5m pre-money valuation, including £400k through a three-week Crowdcube campaign (public launch 10 August), with over 40% secured through pre-commitments and grants including support from Google, Cloudflare, Kylla Investment Partners and angels; founders had invested over £250k. TechRound listed it with SEIS and EIS. Companies House shows VEYR LIMITED incorporated November 2025. Risks: crowded fitness-app market, consumer acquisition costs, Crowdcube window may have ended.
candidate.discoverySignal: July 2026 press release on a £1m round with a Crowdcube campaign; TechRound w/c 17 Aug 2026 lists SEIS & EIS.
candidate.researchRuleMatched: SEIS/EIS seed round under £5m pre-money with a crowdfunding route

founders.name: Adam King
founders.bio: Quoted as CEO and co-founder in the July 2026 release; website says 17 years running a digital agency and co-founded an automotive app that was acquired.

access.notes: Crowdcube portion £400k; the release described a 3-week campaign from 10 Aug 2026, so it may have closed. Founder intro is a fallback route for the rest of the £1m round.

facts.label: Round pre-committed
facts.value: More than 40% via pre-commitments and grants (company release)

openQuestions: Did the Crowdcube campaign close, and is any of the £1m round still open?
Active users, retention and subscription conversion
What does 'support from Google, Cloudflare' mean: credits or equity?

assessment.summary: Right size and price for the family's brief (SEIS/EIS, £4.5m pre-money), but consumer fitness apps are hard and the crowd window may be over.
assessment.bullCase: Strong retention lets VEYR scale subscriptions and licence its engine to gyms or wearables.
assessment.bearCase: Churn and paid acquisition costs prevent a sustainable business.
assessment.whyNow: Round announced July 2026; remaining allocation may be available via founder intro.
diligenceChecklist: Read the live campaign page and offer documents in full
Confirm HMRC advance assurance letter (SEIS/EIS) with the company
Check latest Companies House accounts and confirmation statement
Confirm share class, rights and any nominee structure on the platform
assessment.nextAction: Contact the founders to ask whether the round has room for a direct cheque and request retention data.

candidate.name: Micrima
candidate.teaser: Bristol medtech offering Mi~Scan, a compression- and radiation-free breast density scan; crowdfunding on Crowdcube.
candidate.description: Micrima's Mi~Scan measures breast density without compression or radiation and is paired with Mi~Score risk reporting; its site says the device is CE-marked (Class IIa), ISO 13485 certified, clinically validated with Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, and offered from its Bristol HQ and partner locations. The website banner says 'We're Crowdfunding!' with a link to a Crowdcube campaign; TechRound listed it on Crowdcube in the week of 24 August 2026 but did not state SEIS/EIS. Companies House shows Micrima Limited incorporated 2005. Included as an exception: later-stage and tax relief not confirmed.
candidate.discoverySignal: Company website banner: 'We're Crowdfunding!' linking to Crowdcube; TechRound w/c 24 Aug 2026.

assessment.bullCase: Private breast-density scanning scales via clinic partners and NHS adoption.
assessment.bearCase: Slow adoption after two decades of development; dilutive raises.
